overview:
California's 17th District is a heavily Democratic Bay Area seat, and incumbent Ro Khanna is running for re-election after advancing to the general election. Republican Ritesh Tandon faces steep structural disadvantages: the district's partisan lean favors Democrats by roughly twenty points, and Khanna carries the weight of incumbency in a seat he has held since 2017.

The resource gap is stark. Khanna has raised about $15.3 million and holds more than $16.5 million on hand, while Tandon has raised roughly $57,000 with about $5,000 available, and no outside groups are meaningfully engaged on either side. Prediction markets give Khanna about a 98 percent chance of winning. No public general-election polls or expert ratings exist for this race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals. With the matchup this lopsided, the seat is rated Safe Democratic, though the precise margin carries wide uncertainty.
